identification.name: Carbon Fibre / Epoxy (Unidirectional, ~60 vol%)
identification.common_form_notes: Supplied as prepreg (pre-impregnated, frozen) or dry fabric for wet lay-up / vacuum infusion. Post-cure machining requires diamond or solid carbide tooling due to abrasive fibres.
identification.notes: Properties are for a unidirectional (0°) lamina: standard-modulus carbon fibre (e.g. T300 or AS4, Ef ≈ 230 GPa) in a structural epoxy matrix at approximately 60 vol% fibre. The material is strongly anisotropic — E and strength values given are in the fibre direction (0°). Transverse modulus (90°) is approximately 8–10 GPa and transverse tensile strength approximately 40–60 MPa. For a quasi-isotropic lay-up [0/±45/90]s expect in-plane E ≈ 55–70 GPa and in-plane tensile strength ≈ 400–600 MPa. Thermoset matrix: no melting point; maximum service temperature is set by matrix Tg. Yield strength is not applicable — CFRP is linearly elastic to catastrophic fibre failure.

typical_usage: Aerospace primary structures (fuselage panels, wing skins, control surfaces), high-performance automotive chassis and body panels, robotic arm links, satellite bus structures, bicycle frames, sporting goods (tennis rackets, golf shafts, hockey sticks), and precision optical mounts where near-zero CTE and maximum specific stiffness are required.
